text: In any triangle, the greater angle is subtended by the greater side. Let $ABC$ be a triangle having the angle $ABC$ greater than $BCA$. I say that side $AC$ is also greater than side $AB$.
For if not, $AC$ is certainly either equal to, or less than, $AB$.
assertion: AC is either equal to or less than AB (assuming AC is not greater)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $AC$ is certainly either equal to, or less than, $AB$

text: In fact, $AC$ is not equal to $AB$.
assertion: AC is not equal to AB

text: For then angle $ABC$  would also have been equal to $ACB$ [Prop.~1.5].
assertion: if AC equals AB then angle ABC equals angle ACB (by Prop 1.5)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: angle $ABC$  would also have been equal to $ACB$

assertion: angle ABC is not equal to angle ACB (given)
AC is not equal to AB
AC is not less than AB

text: For then angle $ABC$ would also have been less than $ACB$ [Prop.~1.18].
assertion: if AC is less than AB then angle ABC is less than angle ACB (by Prop 1.18)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: angle $ABC$ would also have been less than $ACB$

assertion: angle ABC is not less than angle ACB (given)
AC is not less than AB

text: But it was  shown that ($AC$) is    not equal (to $AB$) either.
assertion: AC was shown to not be equal to AB (recalling the first case result)

text: Thus, in any triangle, the greater angle is subtended by the greater side. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
